what: Step 1: Fit the initial hazard models
title: Getting started with MultiStateTMLE
text: fit_initial() fits one hazard model per event process, expands data grid observed event times horizon tau, builds discrete state space targeting step works . process specified fit_types code delta column one-sided formula covariates hazard. processes can used covariates name, death hazard depends whether individual fallen ill (z). illness can occur , say individuals risk z z == 0. Exactly one process must censoring process (delta = 0). type process inferred data: death censoring end follow-, illness occurs . default hazards fitted Cox models. Setting fit = "hal" process’s entry uses highly adaptive lasso instead (experimental).
code: fit_types <- list(   z = list(     delta = 2,     model = ~L0,     at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0   ),   death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + z),   censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~L0) )  fit <- fit_initial(illness_death, fit_types = fit_types, tau = 1) fit #> Initial fit of 150 individuals up to tau = 1 #>  #>         name delta     type   model at_risk #>       <char> <num>   <char>  <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:         z     2 one_jump     ~L0    TRUE #> 2:     death     1 terminal ~L0 + z   FALSE #> 3: censoring     0 terminal     ~L0   FALSE

title: Getting started with MultiStateTMLE
text: tmle_alpha() estimates risk target process time tau intervention multiplies intensity z_name alpha. alpha = 1 intervention, observed risk death time 1: printed table gives targeted estimate standard error 95% confidence interval, stored observed$estimate. Halving intensity illness gives: coef() confint() extract estimate confidence intervals levels: Setting alpha = 0 removes illness altogether, alpha > 1 increases intensity.

title: Getting started with MultiStateTMLE
text: calibrate_alpha() solves alpha achieves given exposure risk theta estimates target risk intervention. calibration target given value scale: "absolute": theta = value. "ratio": theta value times observed risk z_name. "difference": theta value plus observed risk z_name. example, risk death risk illness reduced 80% observed value: first table gives calibrated intervention alpha exposure risk theta achieves, second risk death . standard error se accounts alpha estimated, whereas se_crude treats known. target can also expected years life lost tau rather risk death, estimand = "years_lost". exposure still calibrated risk, unless exposure_estimand says otherwise:
code: cal <- calibrate_alpha(   fit,   target = "death",   z_name = "z",   value = 0.8,   scale = "ratio" ) cal #> Calibrated intervention on z #>  #>    quantity  estimate         se      lower     upper #>      <char>     <num>      <num>      <num>     <num> #> 1:    alpha 0.7927238 0.00995552 0.77321133 0.8122363 #> 2:    theta 0.1271303 0.02505712 0.07801922 0.1762413 #>  #> Estimates under the calibrated intervention: #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper   se_crude #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num>      <num> #> 1:  death 0.3199203 0.03864198 0.2441835 0.3956572 0.03866085 calibrate_alpha(   fit,   target = "death",   z_name = "z",   value = 0.8,   scale = "ratio",   estimand = "years_lost" )$estimate #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper   se_crude #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num>      <num> #> 1:  death 0.1644942 0.02295448 0.1195042 0.2094842 0.02295436

title: Getting started with MultiStateTMLE
text: baseline treatment A0, total effect treatment outcome can split part goes effect exposure remainder. calibrated intervention sets treated individuals’ exposure risk placebo, calibrated_contrasts() decomposes total effect : mediated contrast: treatment versus calibrated intervention, calibrated contrast: calibrated intervention versus placebo. illness_death treatment, illustration add randomised treatment actual effect. treatment model given treatment_model, fit_initial() prepares estimates treatment values, = 0 = 1. contrasts computed influence curves fit returns. calibrated arm set = 1 calibrate ratio 1 risk illness placebo, reference_a = 0, risk illness treatment calibrated equal placebo: treatment randomised without effect, confidence intervals three contrasts cover zero, expected.
code: set.seed(1) treated <- illness_death a0 <- rbinom(max(treated$id), 1, 0.5) treated$A0 <- a0[treated$id]  fit_treated <- fit_initial(   treated,   fit_types = list(     z = list(       delta = 2,       model = ~ L0 + A0,       at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0     ),     death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + A0 + z),     censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~L0)   ),   tau = 1,   treatment_model = A0 ~ L0 ) treatment_fit <- tmle_alpha(fit_treated, target = "death", a = 1) placebo_fit <- tmle_alpha(fit_treated, target = "death", a = 0) calibrated_fit <- calibrate_alpha(   fit_treated,   target = "death",   z_name = "z",   value = 1,   scale = "ratio",   a = 1,   reference_a = 0 )  calibrated_contrasts(treatment_fit, placebo_fit, calibrated_fit) #> Decomposition of the effect of a on death into mediated and calibrated contrasts #>  #>    target   contrast   estimate         se       lower      upper #>    <char>     <char>      <num>      <num>       <num>      <num> #> 1:  death      total -0.1405813 0.07724416 -0.29197704 0.01081449 #> 2:  death   mediated -0.0234265 0.01632300 -0.05541899 0.00856599 #> 3:  death calibrated -0.1171548 0.08141345 -0.27672220 0.04241266

title: Causal Inference for Multistate Event Processes via TMLE
text: pipeline three main steps: fit_initial() fits initial (nuisance) hazard models event process data, builds discrete product state space used internally. tmle_alpha() targets initial fit stochastic intensity intervention, scales intensity process alpha (optionally combined intervention baseline treatment). returns TMLE estimate, standard error, optionally efficient influence curve. calibrate_alpha() calibration_curve() calibrate intervention target effect size, calibrated_contrasts() decomposes total treatment effect mediated calibrated contrasts. example, simulated illness-death data illness_death, illness z raises risk death, risk death time 1 intensity illness halved estimated : simulate multistate event history data, see simevent package.
code: library(MultiStateTMLE) fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   fit_types = list(     z = list(       delta = 2,       model = ~L0,       at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0     ),     death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + z),     censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~L0)   ),   tau = 1 )  est <- tmle_alpha(fit, target = "death", alpha = 0.5, z_name = "z") est #> TMLE estimate under alpha = 0.5 on z #> #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:  death 0.3040549 0.03853505 0.2285276 0.3795823 #> #> Initial estimate: 0.3124; converged after 2 iterations

title: Calibrate an intensity intervention to a target value — calibrate_alpha

title: Calibrate an intensity intervention to a target value — calibrate_alpha
code: fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   fit_types = list(     z = list(       delta = 2,       model = ~ L0,       at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0     ),     death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + z),     censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~ L0)   ),   tau = 1 )  # Risk of death under the intervention on z that brings the risk of z # down to 80% of its observed value. cal <- calibrate_alpha(   fit,   target = "death",   z_name = "z",   value = 0.8,   scale = "ratio" ) cal$estimate #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper   se_crude #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num>      <num> #> 1:  death 0.3199203 0.03864198 0.2441835 0.3956572 0.03866085

text: object class calibrated_contrasts, list elements: estimate: data.table one row per contrast (total, mediated calibrated) columns target, contrast, estimate, se, lower upper. target level: target confidence level. checks: list decomposition_error eic_decomposition_error, far estimates influence curves satisfying total = mediated + calibrated, zero numerical error.

title: Decompose a treatment effect into mediated and calibrated contrasts — calibrated_contrasts
code: # illness_death with a randomised treatment A0 added, for illustration. set.seed(1) treated <- illness_death treated$A0 <- rbinom(max(treated$id), 1, 0.5)[treated$id]  fit <- fit_initial(   treated,   fit_types = list(     z = list(       delta = 2,       model = ~ L0 + A0,       at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0     ),     death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + A0 + z),     censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~L0)   ),   tau = 1,   treatment_model = A0 ~ L0 )  # How much of the effect of treatment on death is mediated by its effect # on the risk of z? calibrated_contrasts(   treatment_fit = tmle_alpha(fit, target = "death", a = 1),   placebo_fit = tmle_alpha(fit, target = "death", a = 0),   calibrated_fit = calibrate_alpha(     fit,     target = "death",     z_name = "z",     value = 1,     scale = "ratio",     a = 1,     reference_a = 0   ) ) #> Decomposition of the effect of a on death into mediated and calibrated contrasts #>  #>    target   contrast   estimate         se       lower      upper #>    <char>     <char>      <num>      <num>       <num>      <num> #> 1:  death      total -0.1405813 0.07724416 -0.29197704 0.01081449 #> 2:  death   mediated -0.0234265 0.01632300 -0.05541899 0.00856599 #> 3:  death calibrated -0.1171548 0.08141345 -0.27672220 0.04241266

title: Fit the initial hazard models — fit_initial
text: data data.frame observed event history data long format, one row per event columns id, time delta (integer code process jumped, 0 reserved censoring), plus baseline covariates used fit_types. fit_types named list one entry per event process, named process. entry list elements: delta: process's integer code delta column data. Exactly one process must code 0 (censoring). model: one-sided formula covariates hazard model, ~ L0 + z. processes can used covariates name, case counting process (lagged one event) used. fit: "cox" (default) "hal". at_risk: optional function data returning logical vector, marking rows risk process (e.g. function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0 process can jump ). tau Positive number. Follow-horizon; target parameters evaluated tau. treatment_model Optional logistic regression model baseline treatment, two-sided formula A0 ~ L0. Required arms given. arms Integer vector baseline treatment values (0/1) prepare interventional hazards clever weights . value can passed tmle_alpha(), calibrate_alpha() calibration_curve(). Defaults values, 0:1, treatment_model given. max_count Positive integer. Maximum number jumps tracked per recurrent process state space. derived_vars Named list functions data, deriving additional state variable, named list, can used models fit_types. depend_time Experimental, may change. Named list functions making hazards depend time jump. named state variable: process z jumps , z.k kth jump recurrent process z. adds covariate T.<name>, 0 jump function applied time jump , can used (factor) models fit_types. control named list tuning settings: prune_states (FALSE): TRUE, prune states admissible at_risk functions fit_types. use_exponential (FALSE): TRUE, always transform hazard increments dH probabilities 1 - exp(-dH). Otherwise done increments exceed 1. hal_control named list settings processes fitted fit = "hal", see Details. cores Positive integer. Number cores used parallel::mclapply() predicting hazards across states. verbose Logical. TRUE, print model fits progress.

title: Fit the initial hazard models — fit_initial
text: object class initial_fit, list elements: n: number individuals. tau, treatment_model arms: given (arms default filled ). processes: data.table one row per process columns name, delta, type ("terminal", "recurrent" "one_jump", inferred data), model at_risk (whether at_risk function given). also contains internal elements used tmle_alpha(), among tmp_long (expanded data fitted hazards clever weights) depend_matrix (product state space).

title: Fit the initial hazard models — fit_initial
code: # Illness-death data: z is an illness that can occur once, death is # terminal, and delta = 0 is censoring. head(illness_death) #>   id      time delta         L0 #> 1  1 1.0836890     1  0.2724785 #> 2  2 0.6539194     1  0.3572619 #> 3  3 0.1212156     1 -0.8616620 #> 4  4 1.1416233     2  0.8083350 #> 5  4 3.6778032     1  0.8083350 #> 6  5 1.0962284     2  0.6127352  fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   fit_types = list(     z = list(       delta = 2,       model = ~ L0,       at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0     ),     death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + z),     censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~ L0)   ),   tau = 1 ) fit #> Initial fit of 150 individuals up to tau = 1 #>  #>         name delta     type   model at_risk #>       <char> <num>   <char>  <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:         z     2 one_jump     ~L0    TRUE #> 2:     death     1 terminal ~L0 + z   FALSE #> 3: censoring     0 terminal     ~L0   FALSE

title: Targeted estimation under a stochastic intensity intervention — tmle_alpha
text: initial_fit initial fit, returned fit_initial(). target String. Name target process. z_name String. Name process initial_fit whose intensity alpha scales. Required unless alpha = 1 alpha_list given. alpha Non-negative number. Multiplicative intervention intensity z_name. alpha = 1 intervention. alpha_list Experimental, may change. Optional named list functions, one per process, giving time-varying multiplicative intervention process's intensity. function called columns initial_fit$tmp_long named arguments, e.g. time, baseline covariate L0, process z (number jumps far), must return one non-negative factor per row. example, list(z = function(time) ifelse(time < 0.5, 0.5, 1)) halves intensity z time 0.5. combined alpha z_name. Optional baseline treatment value (0 1) intervene . Must one arms prepared fit_initial(). estimand target parameter: "risk", risk target tau (expected number events recurrent target), "years_lost", expected time lost, .e. integral risk target tau. only_first Logical. TRUE, first target event counts, first jump z_name intervened . target_only_in_state Experimental, may change. Optional function state space initial_fit$depend_matrix, data frame one row per state column per process processes depend (number jumps), returning logical vector marking states target events count. example, function(states) states[["z"]] == 0 counts deaths illness. control named list settings estimate computed: one_step (FALSE): TRUE, return one-step estimator instead iterating TMLE update. block_size (10): positive integer. estimand = "years_lost", integral approximated evaluating risk per block block_size consecutive time points. 1 gives exact integral estimated risk; computation time roughly proportional 1 / block_size. target_by_state (FALSE): TRUE, use state-specific clever covariates targeting step. conv_const (1): positive number. TMLE iterations stop absolute mean efficient influence curve falls conv_const * se / log(n). max_iter (10): maximum number TMLE iterations. min_iter (0): minimum number TMLE iterations checking convergence. truncate_weights (Inf): positive number clever weights intervention truncated. Inf truncation. cores Positive integer. Number cores used parallel::mclapply() per-individual computations. verbose Logical. TRUE, print progress.

title: Targeted estimation under a stochastic intensity intervention — tmle_alpha
text: object class tmle_alpha, list elements: estimate: data.table columns target, estimate, standard error se, bounds lower upper 95% Wald confidence interval. initial_estimate: initial plug-estimate, targeting. method: "tmle", "one_step" control$one_step = TRUE. estimand: given. alpha, z_name : intervention (alpha NULL alpha_list given). eic: list, named target, efficient influence curve, one value per individual. checks: list diagnostics: iter: number iterations. eic_solved_at: absolute mean efficient influence curve. converged: whether iterations converged. warning given . weights: matrix quantiles (columns q50, q90, q99 q100) individuals individual's maximal intervention, censoring treatment weight, product total, weight entering targeting step (rows), positivity diagnostic. intervention weights truncation, treatment weights 1 given. n_truncated: number individuals whose initial intervention weight truncated (0 control$truncate_weights = Inf).
